$comment: Duet's routing opinion, as data so it is inspectable and overridable. A user may override any row in .duet/config.json without editing this file. Claude always orchestrates; this table decides who does the work, not who runs the run. A phase whose category maps to codex AND needs judgement splits into a codex brief followed by a claude phase. It is never one phase with two owners.

codex.why: Establishes ground truth. Better at reading current documentation, real API surfaces and backend detail; less prone to answering from stale recollection.

claude.why: Owns judgement. Better at human-shaped reasoning, structure, and design; worse at recalling which API version is current, which is exactly what the codex brief supplies.

ownership.$comment: The build-time boundary. Routing decides which phase belongs to whom; this decides what each agent may edit once inside one. It exists because a backend model asked to touch the interface tends to write four paragraphs where the button needed two words.

owns: everything the user sees or reads
frontend code, components, layout, styling, motion
all user-facing text: copy, labels, button text, error messages, empty states, onboarding, marketing
claude.note: Claude decides every wording and interface question, including ones Codex raises. An intentional choice stands (standing rule 5).

owns: third-party integrations and their credentials handling
may_not: edit user-facing text, even to correct it
add explanatory copy to a screen because the behaviour seemed unclear
codex.instead: File the concern in the review list with the exact string and why it is wrong. One line. Claude decides, and the run continues either way.

ownership.disputes: A boundary disagreement that survives the rebuttal round joins the single final question round with both positions inline. It never blocks the build.

into.produces: briefing file consumed by the next phase via --append-system-prompt-file

into.consumes: the briefing from the preceding codex phase

mixed_phase_rule.brief_discipline: The brief asks open questions and contains no hypothesis to agree with. See reference/briefing-codex.md, standing rule 8.
mixed_phase_rule.skip_brief_when: The phase needs nothing outside the working directory: pure logic, naming, structural refactors, tradeoff analysis. The router's choice to skip appears on the plan the human approves, so a wrongly skipped brief is visible before anything runs.
mixed_phase_rule.cache: Briefs are cached within a run. A later phase touching the same dependency reuses the existing briefing rather than re-researching it.

deadlock_rule.$comment: Applied to arguments rather than tasks. Used only after the batched debate has run its one rebuttal round.
deadlock_rule.presentation: Both positions with their reasoning inline, so the human decides with the argument in front of them rather than a bare choice.
deadlock_rule.batching: Deadlocks join the single final question round rather than interrupting the run.
